t: Mari, at Tell Hariri in eastern Syria, controlled river traffic on the middle Euphrates for over a thousand years.
In the 24th century BCE it rivalled Ebla; in the 18th century it was ruled by the Amorite kings of the Lim dynasty.
Hammurabi of Babylon conquered it c. 1761 BCE, but its archive of some 20,000 tablets survived in the ruins.
dyk: Zimri-Lim claimed to have built an ice house at Terqa, a feat he said no earlier king had achieved, to keep ice for cooling drinks at court.
ev: Mari is founded at Tell Hariri on the middle Euphrates
Mari’s kings press Ebla, which pays them silver and gold
The second city of Mari is destroyed, probably by Akkad
Yahdun-Lim leads an expedition to the Mediterranean
Shamshi-Adad takes Mari and installs his son Yasmah-Addu
Zimri-Lim regains the throne with the help of Yamhad
Hammurabi of Babylon conquers Mari; its walls are destroyed two years later
Bedouin find a statue on Tell Hariri, leading to French excavations
